description: ISC213 final roadmap: how the twelve lectures fit together, from the principles of transactions to rights, insurance, investing, financing and forbidden gains, with the material to study for each topic, look-alike rulings side by side and a coverage tracker.
lede: Every ruling in ISC213 comes back to the same few reasons: riba, gharar, gambling and injustice. The route starts with the principles that create those reasons, then applies them to rights and insurance, to investing, to financing a purchase, and finally to gains that are forbidden outright.

confusables.title: Commercial vs collaborative insurance
confusables.ask: Is it an exchange for profit or a donation for solidarity?
test: Workers pay into a retirement fund that pays them later. Ruling and system?

confusables.title: Shares vs bonds
confusables.ask: Do you own part of the company or lend it money?
rows: Ownership; return depends on profit; vote
Debt; fixed interest; no vote; paid first
test: A certificate pays a fixed 5% yearly plus a lottery prize.
A bond: prohibited, interest on a loan.

confusables.title: Preferred vs enjoyment shares
confusables.ask: Guaranteed profit, or redeemed early by lottery?
test: Which share type guarantees a return whatever happens?

confusables.title: Standard lease vs lease to own vs installment sale
confusables.ask: Does ownership pass, when, and in how many contracts?
rows: Two contracts; owns at the end
test: You own the car on day one but pay monthly. Which?

confusables.title: Covered vs instant vs revolving card
confusables.ask: Is there a loan, and is there interest?
rows: Loan paid in full by the due date
Permissible if no riba is stipulated
test: A card stipulates interest but you always pay on time.
Not permissible: agreeing to the riba condition is the problem.

confusables.title: Gambling vs betting vs permitted competition
confusables.ask: Chance game, others' effort, or a prize from someone else?
rows: Money on an event decided by others
Third-party prize, no loss to players
test: A shop raises prices and enters buyers in a draw.

confusables.title: MLM vs pyramid scheme
confusables.ask: Real products sold, or money from recruits?
rows: Real products; commission on recruits' sales
Legal in law, forbidden in Islam
Recruitment fees; products fake or a front
test: A distributor earns from her own and her recruits' sales.

confusables.title: Riba al-fadl vs riba al-nasi'ah
confusables.ask: Getting more back, or the same back later?
rows: Excess in an exchange of the same kind
Delay in an exchange that must be immediate
test: Commercial insurance pays back more than you paid. Which riba?
Riba al-fadl (getting the same back later is nasi'ah).
